channel.title: Toby on Fitness Tech — Blog
channel.description: Independent reviews and analysis of fitness technology: Speediance, Tonal, Whoop, Garmin, and more. Real data from a real athlete.

item.title: I Lifted 9 Million Pounds on Tonal. Here's Why I'll Never Buy Another One.
item.description: The device is phenomenal. The company is dreadful. After lifting 9,000,844 pounds on my Tonal and transforming from 250 to 180 pounds, I turned off my membership and found out the hard way what happens when you stop paying.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: The Training That Built My Physique Isn't What I Do Today
item.description: I used Arnold Blueprint PPL to go from 250 to 180 pounds. Now I do full body minus legs. Here's exactly why the training that gets you there isn't the training that keeps you there.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: Speediance V3.1: What Actually Changed
item.description: Progressive overload finally works like it should. Here's what's fixed, what's broken, and what I still want.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: Building an AI Assistant That Manages Everything
item.description: How I built a custom AI on OpenClaw that tracks BJJ, analyzes recovery data, and generates training reports.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: Garmin vs Whoop: The Real Difference
item.description: One tracks everything you do. One tracks how well you recover. Here's which one matters more.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: 1.2 Million Pounds: What 7 Months on the Speediance Actually Taught Me
item.description: I've logged 125 workouts and 1,296,447 lbs of total volume on the Speediance Gym Monster 2S since July 2025. Here's what the data actually revealed — the patterns I didn't expect, the software that nearly broke me, and why I still have two of these machines in my house.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: When WHOOP Says 18%: What I Do (And Don't Do) On a Red Day
item.description: February 11, 2026: WHOOP recovery 18%, HRV 18.7ms, 3.5 hours of sleep, 8Sleep score 61. Here's the exact decision tree I run through — and what my AI assistant recommended with 77.8% confidence.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: The Speediance Safety Start Problem (And Why I Turned It Off)
item.description: Speediance shipped Safety Start in V3.1 and called it a safety feature. It's not. Here's what it actually does, what it does to your range of motion, and the firmware side effects that came with it.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: Why I Use Both Garmin and WHOOP (And What Each One Is Actually For)
item.description: I wear a Garmin 265S and a WHOOP 5.0 simultaneously. They serve completely different functions — one tells me what I did, the other tells me how well I recovered. Conflating them is how people make bad training decisions.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: The Speediance 1RM System Is More Complicated Than You Think (But Also Better)
item.description: A user online claimed the Speediance 2S can't do 260 lbs outside of Free Lift. He was dead wrong — and proving it live sent me down a rabbit hole into how the PR and progressive overload system actually works under the hood.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: I Saw Mike Israetel Compete as a Brown Belt. Here's My Actual Take.
item.description: The internet has decided Mike Israetel isn't a real BJJ black belt. Greg Doucette and Ariel Helwani have weighed in. As a brown belt who actually watched Israetel compete three years ago, I have some things to say about all of this.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: 242 to 188 Pounds: The Honest Truth About How I Actually Did It
item.description: I went from 242 to 188 lbs in six months in 2023. Someone commented they wanted my physique so they could buy a Speediance. I owe them honesty: here's every drug, every protocol, every data point. Nothing natural about it — and I'm not pretending otherwise.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: I Built an AI That Reads My Recovery Data Every Morning — Here's What It Actually Outputs
item.description: I spent a week building a custom fitness intelligence system on OpenClaw that pulls from six data sources and generates a morning training recommendation before I wake up. Here's the real output, the decision logic, and what I've learned from running it daily.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: I Spent $5,000 On the Speediance 2S. Here's What Nobody Tells You.
item.description: The 2S is nearly silent in standby mode. The original sounds like a late 90s gaming PC. And that extra 40 pounds of resistance? It feels like 60. Here's my unfiltered first look after getting both machines home.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: Speediance Modes Explained: Why I Use Stamina For Everything
item.description: Gain Muscle, Stamina, Strength, and Custom — what each mode actually does, why Custom mode can ruin your 1RM tracking, and the exact settings I use for warm-ups that actually work.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: Speediance's Lost Feature: What V3 Took Away (And Why It Matters)
item.description: The V3 software update removed a partner mode that was literally in all of Speediance's original demo videos. I demo it with my daughter Lily on the V2 machine and explain why the feature was better than what Tonal offers — and why it's still missing in V3.1.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters

item.title: I Stopped Training Legs — Here's What Happened
item.description: I built my physique with Push-Pull-Legs. Now I do full body minus legs and lift 41,500 lbs per session. Here's exactly why I made the switch, what changed in my programming, and why the Lunar Challenge forced me to reinvent my training split mid-stream.
item.author: Toby Glenn Peters
